newsitem.title: FRANCE: Zaire rebel spokesman vows to hunt Mobutu in exile.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebel spokesman vows to hunt Mobutu in exile.

text.p: The spokesman in France of Zaire's new rulers vowed on Sunday to hunt ousted president Mobutu Sese Seko "wherever he goes" in exile.

"With us, he will never be in peace. Wherever he goes, we will find him," Zamba Afri Kounyen, the spokesman in France for Laurent Kabila's rebels told radio France-Info in an interview. He warned France against giving shelter to Mobutu, who owns a mansion at Roquebrune Cap Martin on the French Riviera.

"The coordination of committees of vigilance and support to Kabila wants quite officially to tell the French government that we would regard it as an unfriendly act for our people if France accepted that Mobutu take refuge in France," Kounyen said.

Mobutu and his family flew into exile in Morocco after the rebels overran the Zairean capital Kinshasa on Saturday and Kabila proclaimed himself head of state. Kounyen said the allies of Mobutu had plundered Zaire. "We regard them as criminals who must be detained and taken to trial by a people's court," he said.

French media speculated that Mobutu could go on from Morocco to Lichtenstein and later to his French Riviera villa, where he made several stays to recover from cancer surgery over the past few months as the rebels were gradually taking over his country.

France backed Mobutu long after other western powers dropped him, but French officials say they are not aware of his plans. Commentators say Paris is unlikely to offer him shelter, at least before the May 25-June 1 parliamentary election, for fear that his presence would become a campaign issue.
